name: Kettlebell American Swing (Overhead)
description: The kettlebell American swing extends the traditional Russian swing by swinging the kettlebell fully overhead to lockout, rather than stopping at shoulder height. This demands greater shoulder stability and hip power through a larger arc. The overhead finish requires the core and lats to stabilize forcefully at the top. It is popular in CrossFit and conditioning contexts, though it demands solid shoulder mobility and strength before attempting.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet hip- to shoulder-width, kettlebell on the floor between feet. Hinge at the hips, grab the handle with both hands, tilt the bell back.
execution.setup_instructions: Confirm full shoulder flexion range before attempting. Use a lighter kettlebell than your Russian swing weight.
steps: Step 1: Hike the kettlebell back between the legs with a hip hinge.
Step 2: Drive the hips explosively forward, standing tall, and let the bell swing upward.
Step 3: Continue the arc overhead until the bell is fully above the head, arms locked, biceps near the ears.
Step 4: Control the descent, let the bell swing back between the legs, and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at hip extension, inhale on the downswing.
common_mistakes: Pressing the kettlebell overhead with arm strength rather than hip drive
safety_considerations: Requires overhead shoulder mobility — screen before prescribing
Do not attempt with shoulder impingement
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip hinge to full overhead lockout with straight arms.
